device: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition
objective: Improve topology-event recovery and long-horizon stability without changing continuous Gaussian decoding or the fixed resident-row budget.

implemented_training_contract.optimizer_update_cadence: once per outer step after accumulating TBPTT and event-segment gradients
implemented_training_contract.checkpoint_selection: minimum seed/horizon PSNR - drift_penalty * worst per-seed cross-horizon PSNR drift

target2d_correctness.issue: The former batched custom Target2D dispatch corrupted interior rows and produced a NaN tail row at quality scale.
target2d_correctness.resolution: Keep the recurrent rollout batched but dispatch one device Target2D custom op per sample row and concatenate its outputs.

scale_limit_audit.effective_range_owner: The graded material seed layout preallocates fixed continuous-scale slots according to seed_measure_ratio; topology relocates those slots.
scale_limit_audit.conclusion: No measured candidate touched a material, render, interaction, or scale-feature clamp.

broad_results.name: ratio4_drift_aware_checkpoint_selection
broad_results.decision: rejected after an unseen broad seed escaped the 16-seed checkpoint gate

training_throughput.interpretation: Exact event splitting and one-update-per-outer-step training retained the established throughput range. The optional paired degradation render costs approximately 6-10 percent.

remaining_boundaries: The original ratio4 checkpoint remains the quality leader because no event-aware candidate improved both broad quality and worst-seed drift.
Checkpoint evaluation over large seed-horizon matrices remains too slow and must move to an optimized batched no-grad executor before it can become an every-checkpoint gate.
Training reports scheduled topology opportunities; broad validation separately reports device-accepted exchanges.
The recurrent rule has not learned robust dynamics over the 2.5x and 3x radius material distributions even though those distributions do not saturate hard limits.
next_step: Train for broad stochastic long-horizon recovery with an efficient batched no-grad evaluator and held-out tail selection; do not widen scale ranges or tune topology schedules again until that gate improves.
